speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe exactly where the pain starts and how it radiates through your arm? Also, have you noticed any specific movements or positions that worsen these symptoms or the weakness?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any numbness or weakness in your legs, or have you noticed any changes in your bladder or bowel control? Additionally, does the pain worsen when you extend your neck backward?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the presence of fasciculations, absent reflexes, and bilateral hand weakness, I need to rule out lower motor neuron involvement. REQUEST TEST: EMG_and_Nerve_Conduction_Studies.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the EMG is normal, we can rule out lower motor neuron diseases like ALS. Given your history of diabetes, I suspect a multifocal motor neuropathy or cervical radiculopathy, but I need to visualize the spine. REQUEST TEST: Cervical_MRI.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI of the spine reveals a syrinx (cavity) within the spinal cord extending from the cervical to the upper thoracic region.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of a syrinx explains your symptoms, which is consistent with syringomyelia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Syringomyelia
